reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent source-semantic review against the live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP view and Radare2 6.2.0 on retail igi.exe (SHA-256 dea34892...); the candidate translation unit was recompiled with the repository -O3 -DNDEBUG flags and its object symbol compared with the body recorded for the previous source digest.
source_revision: worktree HEAD 5a3b6e40521b2159f6dce7e8ecbeafb8fe3b9b91 plus the uncommitted Qvm_ReportError correction; bound by engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp sha256 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f
review_basis: The current engine/src/retail/script/qvm_native_loader.cpp hashes to 48ae1e2700dfc8738d9ea1a31178495ff821c3bed69ac189263a88eebac8359f. The retail entry was re-read through the live Binary Ninja view and independently recovered with Radare2 on 2026-10-23; both live graphs are identical to the bound artifacts, so the recorded CFG is current. The candidate was recompiled from that source; its object symbol body was compared with the body compiled from the previous source digest 655494c9... and is instruction-identical after relocation resolution, proving the Qvm_ReportError edit did not alter this function. This review supersedes the earlier evidence that was stale against the current source digest.

retail_function.name: Qvm_Load
retail_function.summary: 0x004B80B0-0x004B83C5 (791 bytes), 21 basic blocks / 29 edges, cdecl void*(const char* path). Non-debug path: Resource_FileExists(path), Resource_Load(path,&size), allocate a 0x94-byte zeroed object, Qvm_SetGlobalState(0), store the loaded buffer at +0x80, size at +0x84 and the path at +0x00. Debug path: copy the path, replace the extension with .qvm, call Sys_PushStack_16 (0x004B6440) / Sys_PopStack_16 (0x004B6490) and resolve the standalone via Sys_ResolveSymbol_28 (0x004BD220), and on the .qas path run QScript cleanup (0x004B1AC0), ParseAndAssemble (0x004BBCB0) and Assemble (0x004BB270) before reallocating and resolving; store the standalone pointer at +0x8C and the byte flag 1 at +0x90.

comparison.changed_bytes: 26 section relocation addends plus the Qvm_ReportError rel32; all resolve to the same symbols/literals

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja and Radare2 both recover 0x004B80B0-0x004B83C5 with 21 blocks / 29 edges; the live re-read matches the bound artifacts exactly (similarity 1.000). The candidate symbol igi::retail::script::Qvm_Load(char const*) is the body implementing that entry, 1136 bytes including alignment padding; the source provenance comment claiming 33 blocks/50 edges is stale and is not used here.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Retail reads the single stack argument at [esp+0x130] into EBP at entry and forwards it to Resource_FileExists/Resource_Load and the debug-path helpers; the candidate declares const char* qvm_path in that position. cdecl and the 32-bit pointer return agree (Binary Ninja int32_t*, Radare2 int32_t arg_130h, candidate void*).

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The allocation size 0x94 and alignment 4, the object offsets +0x00/+0x80/+0x84/+0x88/+0x8C/+0x90, the 0x100 and 0x80 path buffers, the 5-byte ".qvm"/".qas" copies including the NUL, and the zero-fill of 0x25 dwords are all present at the corresponding points. The candidate writes a 32-bit 1 at +0x90 where retail writes the single byte 1; because the 0x94-byte block was just zeroed and bytes +0x91..+0x93 are not otherwise written, the resulting bytes are identical.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: The reachable call sequence matches: Resource_FileExists/Resource_Load, Mem_Alloc(0x94,4), memset, Qvm_SetGlobalState(0), QScript_Cleanup/ParseAndAssemble/Assemble and Qvm_Cleanup on the debug path, Sys_ResolveSymbol_28 on both resolve paths, then Mem_Alloc/memset again before the final resolve. The debug helpers and the heap/stack helpers are injectable null-default boundaries, recorded below. Two source-level differences exist after Qvm_ReportError (the failed-resolve path omits retail Mem_DeAllocFn(result) at 0x004B833B; the QScript_Assemble failure path returns nullptr instead of retail mov eax,ebx at 0x004B835E). In this port Qvm_ReportError ends that path in a non-returning halt, and in the retail game the installed exit callback terminates the process, so neither difference can execute in the current build; they are recorded as limitations rather than claimed as matches.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Pointer, integer and string handling only; no floating-point data or instructions.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The 0x94-byte zeroed object, the dword fields at +0x80/+0x84/+0x88/+0x8C and the flag at +0x90 match the retail offsets and widths. The candidate zero-initialises the 0x100 and 0x80 path buffers before copying the string; retail leaves them uninitialised, but the copied NUL-terminated text and every scanned byte are identical, so the extra zeroing is not observable through the retail reads. No store outside the allocated object.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Success returns the allocated object in both. Early failures (missing resource, failed load, null resolve before allocation) return 0/null in both. The debug-path ParseAndAssemble failure calls Qvm_Cleanup, reports and returns 0 in both. The failed final resolve reports and returns 0 in both. The QScript_Assemble failure returns the allocated object in retail and nullptr in the candidate; that path is reachable only if Qvm_ReportError returns, which the current port never does, and it is recorded as a limitation.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports int32_t*(void* arg1) and Radare2 recovers cdecl with one stack argument; the candidate declares void* Qvm_Load(const char*). The retail return value is a pointer to the script object; the candidate returns the same byte buffer pointer, so the 32-bit pointer return and the single stack argument are preserved.

limitations: No paired retail/candidate game-process runtime capture exists for this address; runtime_tests and behavioral are intentionally absent and RUNTIME_TESTED/VERIFIED are not claimed.
The CFG agreement cited here is Binary Ninja vs Radare2 on the retail image; cfg_similarity 1.0 is not a candidate-vs-retail CFG score, and the candidate machine CFG was not compared for isomorphism.
The candidate object was rebuilt and hashed, but the image was not linked by this review; no linked-image or receipt claim is made.

The compiled object body differs from the body recorded for 655494c9... only in relocation addends: 27 section relocations plus the direct call to Qvm_ReportError. 8 of the 27 addends moved because the port-owned globals/strings shifted (.bss g_5c8bec 0x14->0x20 and g_5c8bf0 0x10->0x1c, .data g_a965a0 0x0->0x4, .rdata kExtQvm 0x20->0x1c, its NUL byte 0x24->0x20, and the format string 0x3->0x0); the other 19 are unchanged. After resolving each addend back to the symbol or literal it names, the 300-entry object disassembly is identical. No instruction, branch, call target or field offset changed.

The debug/.qas branch calls Sys_PushStack_16, Sys_PopStack_16, Sys_ResolveSymbol_28, QScript_Cleanup, QScript_ParseAndAssemble and QScript_Assemble through injectable boundaries with null defaults; the default candidate therefore skips those calls rather than performing the retail callees. The integration must install the boundaries.

Two post-report source differences are known and NOT claimed as equivalent: on the failed final resolve the retail body calls Mem_DeAllocFn(result) at 0x004B833B after Qvm_ReportError and the candidate returns without releasing the object; on the QScript_Assemble failure the retail body returns the allocated object (0x004B835E mov eax,ebx) and the candidate returns nullptr. Both sit after Qvm_ReportError, which halts in this port (no writer for g_a43e70) and terminates the retail game through the installed exit callback, so they are unreachable in the current build; if an error callback is ever installed they become reachable and must be corrected.

The source provenance comment's callee-chain sentence is mangled (it names Binary Ninja and Radare2 as callees) and its 33 blocks/50 edges counts are stale; the refreshed evidence is 21 blocks / 29 edges. The comment is out of scope for this rebind.

The binary_ninja and radare2 evidence signatures bound here were re-derived from the current artifacts (int32_t*(void* arg1) and fcn.004b80b0 (int32_t arg_130h);); the manifest previously said 'not restated'.
